Premonition for your Mac

A helper that lives on your laptop. You talk to it like a chat, and it can look things up, read pages, use your apps and keep an eye on things for you. Nothing you say leaves your computer. Setting it up takes about ten minutes, most of it waiting.

1Open Terminal

Press Cmd + Space (the Spotlight search), type Terminal, and press Return. A window with a blinking cursor opens. That is fine and safe; you only need it this once.

2Paste this one line

Copy the line below, click inside the Terminal window, press Cmd + V, then Return.

curl -fsSL https://github.com/BenjaminHannan/learner/raw/main/desk/dist/install-mac.sh | bash

It prints a few friendly progress lines (download, install, finish). Wait for "Done." The app downloads (about 100 MB), goes into your Applications folder, and opens by itself. You do not need a password and nothing else gets installed.

If it says something went wrong, read the plain sentence it prints, check that the Wi-Fi is on, and paste the same line again. It is safe to run as many times as you like, and it also installs updates.

3The first start downloads its brain

The first time, a progress screen appears inside the window while Premonition downloads its small language model. This happens once, and the model then lives on your Mac.

WhatSize
The program that runs the modelabout 16 MB
The language model (LFM3, small and quick)about 1 GB
If your Wi-Fi drops, open Premonition again (or press Try again). It carries on where it stopped. Plan on a few minutes on good Wi-Fi, and leave the lid open while it works.

Then it asks a few setup questions: what you want Glims (your helpers) for, how much it should ask you first (pick Ask first to begin with), and any jobs to repeat on a schedule. You can skip any of it and change it later in Settings.

macOS will ask for two permissions

Your Mac keeps apps from watching or controlling it until you say yes. Premonition shows a small card that walks you through it. Both are optional, and you can turn them off again whenever you like.

  • Screen Recording: lets Glim see your screen when you ask it to look at something or a job needs it.
  • Accessibility: lets Glim click and type in other apps for you, only when you ask it to.

In System Settings, open Privacy & Security, find the permission, and switch Premonition on. macOS may ask you to quit and reopen the app afterwards: say yes.

If macOS says it "can't verify" Premonition or "can't be opened": the installer normally avoids this. If it shows up anyway, open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message about Premonition, click Open Anyway, and enter your Mac password. You only do this once. (Or paste the install line into Terminal again.)

Chatting

  • Type what you want and press Return. Ask questions, ask it to look something up, or give it a job.
  • The top bar has Auto, Think and Fast. Fast answers quickest. Think takes longer on harder questions.
  • Ask first means Glim checks with you before it clicks or types on your computer. Hands-off lets it go ahead (it still asks before anything risky).
  • Press Option + Space from any app to show or hide Premonition. Quit for real with Cmd + Q.
Passwords stay with you. If a page needs a sign-in, Premonition opens it for you to type in yourself. Glim never sees what you type there and will never ask for a password in chat.

This is a small model that runs on your own laptop (small enough for an 8 GB Mac). It is quick and private, but it can make mistakes. Check anything important. Sleep, the way Glim learns overnight, is not available on this Mac yet.

Privacy

  • The model runs on your Mac. Your chats are not sent to any AI company.
  • The only internet traffic is what you ask for (searching or opening a page) and the one-time downloads.
  • Chats and memories live in ~/Library/Application Support/Premonition.

If something is odd

  • It says Offline: the model is still starting (it takes a moment after launch). Wait a minute, or click Offline in the top bar to start it.
  • The download stops: open the app again; it resumes. If it says it cannot start the model, press Try again.
  • Slow answers: Fast mode helps, and closing heavy apps frees memory.
  • Update: paste the install line into Terminal again.

Uninstall

  1. Quit Premonition (Cmd + Q).
  2. Drag Premonition from your Applications folder to the Bin.
  3. To erase everything it saved and downloaded, also delete the folder ~/Library/Application Support/Premonition (this removes your chats and the 1 GB model).
